record.summary: Harish Verma gave Rs. 4,50,000 to his friend Sameer Joshi in January last year for equipment. The loan was verbal, with a promise to repay within 12 months. Only Rs. 40,000 was received by bank transfer in April; Sameer claims he repaid the rest in cash in three installments (March, June, September). Harish says he got no cash, though he once said he might have received something in June. WhatsApp messages show Sameer saying in October he would clear the balance soon, while Harish’s June message "got the amount, thanks" is ambiguous. No written agreement exists. Harish wants to sue for recovery.
record.goal: File a recovery suit for the loan amount and assess the strength of the case.
questions: What was the exact date (and if possible, a copy) of the written demand Harish sent after the loan term?
Did Harish receive any cash receipt, bank slip, or any other acknowledgment for the alleged cash repayments in March, June or September?
Can Harish clarify what amount he referred to in his June WhatsApp message "got the amount, thanks"?
Are there any witnesses (e.g., the mutual friend) who can attest to the timing or amount of any cash that Harish actually received?
Did Sameer ever provide a written or electronic acknowledgment (email, message, receipt) that the cash withdrawals were used to repay the loan?
contradictions: Harish first said he might have received cash around June, but later stated he received no cash at all.
Sameer claims the entire loan was repaid in cash, yet bank records show only Rs. 40,000 transferred and no cash credits to Harish.
Sameer's October WhatsApp message indicates the balance was still pending, contradicting his claim of full repayment.
Harish's June message "got the amount, thanks" is ambiguous and does not specify the amount, conflicting with his later claim of receiving nothing.
evidence: Bank statement: transfer of Rs. 4,50,000 from Harish to Sameer on 12 January last year (narration "loan").
Bank statement: incoming transfer of Rs. 40,000 from Sameer to Harish in April.
Sameer's bank statement: cash withdrawals of Rs. 1,50,000 each in March, June, September, with concurrent equipment payments.
WhatsApp thread: Sameer's October message "will clear the balance soon, tight on cash".
Harish's June WhatsApp message "got the amount, thanks".
Mutual friend’s recollection: heard Harish say "Sameer is paying me back slowly".

follow_up.question: When and where did you last see or use the missing item?
follow_up.why: This narrows the time and place to check for records or witnesses.

evidence_plan.heading: Scene and evidence review
evidence_plan.safety: Get to safety and seek medical or police help if needed. Do not enter or alter a scene to gather evidence. Leave physical collection to the authorities.
prompts: Where did each event happen, and what was the last confirmed time before it?
What did you actually see or hear? Where were you, and what could you see from there?
What was already different when you arrived, and what changed afterward? Say if you are unsure.

suggestions.title: Item identification and last known location
suggestions.look_for: Look for a serial number, receipt, older photo or repair record. Write down when and where you last saw the item and when you noticed it missing.
suggestions.why: This can establish which item is missing and narrow the time window. It cannot identify who took it by itself.
suggestions.action: Save copies of records you own. If a device location service shows a location, share it with police instead of going there yourself.

suggestions.title: Footage from an authorised keeper
suggestions.look_for: If cameras cover the relevant place, note their owner and the narrow time window from your timeline.
suggestions.why: It may show movement or timing. A camera can have blind spots or an inaccurate clock.
suggestions.action: Ask the owner or investigating officer to preserve the original recording promptly. Record your request. Use only footage you are authorised to access.

suggestions.title: Purchase, promised terms and communications
suggestions.look_for: Look for the order confirmation, invoice, payment record and relevant warranty or service terms. Keep the complete email or chat thread.
suggestions.why: These can show what was purchased, what was promised and what resolution the seller offered.
suggestions.action: Keep the original files or exports. Record dates and ask for copies from the seller or platform if you do not have them.

suggestions.title: Condition of the product or work
suggestions.look_for: If safe, note the model or order number, the fault and when it appeared. Keep existing dated photos, service requests or repair reports.
suggestions.why: A dated record helps distinguish what you observed from a possible explanation of the fault.
suggestions.action: Leave suspected electrical or other hazardous damage to a qualified person. Ask the repair provider for a written report if they inspect it.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
